candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate active-assisted ROM from active and passive ROM based on how much of the movement the client can perform independently.

options.A: Passive range of motion means the client independently contracts the muscles while the nurse only observes.
options.B: Active range of motion means the nurse moves the joint through the prescribed arc while the client remains relaxed.
options.C: Active-assisted range of motion means the client initiates movement and receives help to complete the prescribed range that cannot yet be reached alone.
options.D: Resistive range of motion means the joint is moved without muscle contraction while the extremity remains completely relaxed.

candidate.rationale: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals distinguishes active, passive, and active-assisted range of motion. Active-assisted ROM is used when the client can initiate or perform part of the movement but needs external assistance to complete the prescribed range. This exactly matches the stem.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Active-assisted ROM involves client-initiated movement supplemented by assistance to complete a range the client cannot accomplish independently.
candidate.source_locator: Mobility/Range-of-Motion section — definitions of active, passive, and active-assisted ROM.
